ENERGY STAR Certified Residential Clothes Dryers

notes: The datasets give annual energy use (kWh/yr) per certified model but do not state a per-model cycles-per-year or per-cycle kWh figure, so kwhPerCycle and cyclesPerYear are null for every row here; the per-model annual figure (kwhPerYear) already reflects the manufacturer-reported result of the DOE federal test procedure, which assumes a fixed number of cycles per year (below) to derive that annual figure from a measured per-cycle energy use.

Dishwashers: ENERGY STAR states the federal test procedure assumes 215 cycles per year (about 4 times a week) for calculating annual dishwasher energy use. Source: https://www.energystar.gov/products/dishwashers/key_product_criteria (read 2026-10-05).

Clothes dryers: in the DOE test procedure amendment effective for products in Jan 2011, DOE revised the assumed clothes dryer usage from 416 cycles/year to 283 cycles/year (91% usage factor applied to average household loads), based on 2005 RECS data. Source: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2011/01/06/2010-32118/energy-conservation-program-for-consumer-products-test-procedures-for-clothes-dryers-and-room-air (read 2026-10-05).

Clothes washers: the March 2012 DOE final test-procedure rule set the assumed washer usage at 295 cycles per year (updated down from 392), based on 2005 RECS data; a later 2022 DOE final rule (test procedures for residential and commercial clothes washers) revised the assumed annual cycles further, to 234 cycles per year, reflecting updated usage data. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2010/09/21/2010-22225/energy-conservation-program-for-consumer-products-test-procedure-for-residential-clothes-washers and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2022/06/01/2022-10715/energy-conservation-program-test-procedures-for-residential-and-commercial-clothes-washers (both read 2026-10-05).
